subject: Architecture
title: The Edge: The Smartest Building on Earth
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Edge: The Smartest Building on Earth usable.

hook.text: The Edge in Amsterdam was called the world's smartest building. It knows where you sit and what you like.

buildup.text: 28,000 sensors monitor light, temperature, humidity, and occupancy in real time across every floor.

discovery.text: Workers have no assigned desks. An app directs them to spaces matching their schedule and preferences.

twist.text: The building generates more electricity than it uses — solar panels on the south facade power everything.

climax.text: BREEAM gave it a score of 98.4% — the highest sustainability rating ever awarded to any office building.

punchline.text: The building knows you better than you know the building.

quiz.question: How many sensors does The Edge use to monitor conditions?

details.summary: The Edge in Amsterdam, designed by PLP Architecture for Deloitte, uses 28,000 sensors to manage its environment. Workers connect via a smartphone app that finds them a desk based on their schedule, adjusts lighting and temperature to their preferences, and even guides their parking when they arrive.
details.whyItMatters: The Edge demonstrates how smart technology transforms the workplace experience. Its personalized environment improves comfort and productivity while using 70% less electricity than a typical office building through data-driven optimization.
takeaways: 28,000 sensors manage lighting, temperature, and space allocation
A smartphone app personalizes each worker's environment daily
Uses 70% less electricity than a typical office building

faq.question: How does the app personalize the workspace?
faq.answer: The app learns individual preferences for lighting, temperature, and desk type. When workers arrive, it assigns desks based on their schedule — quiet zones for focus work, collaborative areas for team days. Lights and temperature adjust automatically when the worker sits down.

faq.question: How does The Edge use so little energy?
faq.answer: LED panels powered by Ethernet cables provide both light and data connectivity. An aquifer thermal energy storage system heats and cools using underground water. Rooftop and facade solar panels generate energy.
